title: mantissa-glitch-lab-notes
content:
Quick context
- Personal scratchpad capturing an odd, reproducible NaN/quality regression that appears when switching to a constrained INT8 backend on a distilled GPT-style 6-layer model (internal name: tiny-6). Happens only on some seeds and with certain calibration settings.
- Repro machine: dev-gpu-03 (A100-40GB), driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.8, PyTorch 2.2.0, custom inference runtime v0.9.3, cutlass 2.9 (patched).

Initial symptom
- Generations start fine but after ~1200 tokens a NaN appears in logits. Downstream softmax produces NaN probabilities and decoding stops. No obvious OOMs. Logs show floating-point invalids flagged in third attention block.
- When using BF16/FP32 serving path, no NaNs and quality matches baseline. INT8 and FP8 reductions sometimes produce NaNs.

Commands I ran (shortened)
- baseline FP32 run: python tools/run_inference.py --model tiny-6 --dtype fp32 --batch 1 --seed 42
- quantized evaluation (calib using 1024 tokens): python tools/quant_eval.py --model tiny-6 --quant int8 --calib 1024 --batch 1 --seed 42
- emulate int8 with fake-quant: python tools/quant_eval.py --model tiny-6 --quant fake-int8 --calib 1024 --batch 1 --seed 42
- fp8 candidate: python tools/quant_eval.py --model tiny-6 --quant fp8 --format e4m3 --calib 4096 --batch 1 --seed 7

Representative error snippet (from runtime stderr)
- RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in add (aten::add)
- RuntimeError: NAN encountered in attention_kv_cache (block 3, layer 2)
- stack:
  at runtime/infer_kernels.cu:line 1181
  at runtime/attention.cu:line 482
  at tools/run_inference.py:line 227

What I checked so far
1) Seed sensitivity
- seed 42: NaN after ~1200 tokens (INT8 calib=1024)
- seed 7: no NaN for INT8 calib=1024 but FP8 e4m3 gets NaN at ~800 tokens
- seed 123: sometimes NaN, inconsistent.
Conclusion: stochasticity matters — likely due to calibration/activation clipping and/or RNG in fake-quant.

2) Calibration size and scheme
- calib 256 -> NaN earlier (~300 tokens)
- calib 1024 -> NaN at ~1200 tokens
- calib 4096 -> mostly stable for INT8 but FP8 still unstable for some seeds
- scheme: per-channel symmetric vs per-tensor asymmetric. Per-channel symmetric helps a lot on linear weight quant but attention projection scales still problematic.

3) Rounding mode / quant sim
- Round-to-nearest (default): NaN triggered.
- Stochastic rounding (sim): fewer NaNs but worse perplexity when not NaN. Hypothesis: stochastic rounding hides a bias that prevents extreme activations from crossing subnormal/overflow thresholds.

4) Denorms/subnorm handling
- Enabling denorms-flush-to-zero on runtime made NaN incidence worse -> suggests tiny nonzero values in intermediary arrays are semantically relevant (not just noise).
- Clamping activations to [-1e4, +1e4] reduced NaN frequency but sometimes silently degrades outputs.

5) Layer-localized: which layer fails
- Traced with extra logging: first NaN observed inside attention softmax in layer index 2 (0-based). The pre-softmax logits include a couple of very large positive values (~1e7) in the blocked int8 path, which makes exp overflow and inf -> NaN after subtract.
- In FP32 path, the logits max out at ~25, so no overflow. So quant / dequant mismatch seems to introduce outliers.

6) Activation histograms
- Captured per-layer activation histograms during calibration and eval (ascii histograms noted below).
- Layer 2 pre-softmax logits (INT8 calibrated): long left tail around -1e3 and occasional spikes to +1e6 (rare). Spike frequency correlates with NaN incidence.

Experiment log (short table)
- EXP-01: int8, calib 1024, per-channel symmetric, seed 42 -> NaN @1202 tokens
- EXP-02: int8, calib 4096, per-channel symmetric, seed 42 -> stable (no NaN)
- EXP-03: int8, calib 1024, per-tensor asymmetric, seed 42 -> NaN earlier
- EXP-04: fake-int8, same seed -> no NaN (suggests runtime kernel quant/dequant path bug vs emulation)
- EXP-05: fp8 e4m3, calib 4096, seed 7 -> NaN @803 tokens
- EXP-06: int8 plus clip 1e3 -> no NaN but KL to FP32 increases by 0.18 (bad)

Hypotheses (ordered)
A) Kernel-level bug in int8 dequant path: dequant -> matmul mismatch produces a small number that gets scaled up (mantissa corruption) leading to outliers. Evidence: fake-int8 (emulation in FP32) doesn't show NaN.
B) Calibration failure: calibration didn't see rare outlier activation distributions in tail; quant scales too small and rare inputs saturate to extreme int values when actual eval sees them. Evidence: larger calib reduces NaN incidence.
C) Rounding/accumulator overflow: int8 kernels use int32 accumulators with per-block reductions and mixed precision conv; pathological accumulation order could overflow before final rescale.
D) FP8 layout/exp bias handling: e4m3 exp/bias handling in our FP8 code maybe flips sign when handling subnormals -> NaN.

Quick triage runs to differentiate A vs B
- Re-run with fused kernel replaced by reference GEMM (FP32 dequant->GEMM->quant) on the same data path: no NaNs. Points to A (kernel bug) or C (accumulator overflow in optimized kernel) rather than pure calibration.
- Inserted a debug assert after dequant: check for finite values and magnitude < 1e8. Found a handful of values exactly 1.545e35 (suspicious large float close to huge round numbers) right after dequant.

Repro mini-case creation notes
- Create input batch that triggers the spike: run sample generation with deterministic prompt and record per-token pre-softmax max. Use seed 42; save the token sequence up to the NaN. Then replay with logging enabled in exact same hardware to capture kernel inputs.

Workarounds discovered so far
- Increase calibration corpus to 4096 examples: reduces probability of NaN (less convenient).
- Add a small soft clip to pre-softmax logits: x_clipped = sign(x) * min(abs(x), 500.0) — masks bug but changes model outputs.
- Fallback to BF16 for flagged requests by tracking per-request metrics (adds complexity).

Next diagnostic steps (todo)
- Build instrumented kernel with prints for dequant output for the failing block (only on dev-gpu-03 to keep deterministic).
- Run single-layer unit tests with artificially constructed weights that amplify accumulation paths to test int32 overflow hypothesis.
- Dump raw int8 integer buffers before scale/rescale to examine values.
- Re-run with alternate cutlass config (disable knl-opt reorder) to see whether scheduling affects reproducibility.
- Try run with relaxed fp16 accumulation path (if available) to see whether switching accumulator width affects NaNs.

Notes for PRs/communication
- If this is kernel-bug A/C, we need to isolate a minimal repro and open a PR to runtime with regression test that runs the sequence above and asserts finiteness. Include saved token trace as fixture.
- If calibration B is root cause, add a 'tail-aware' calibration option: detect once-per-calib extremely large activations and expand calibration or use percentile-based clipping (99.999 quantile).

Random observations (might be noise)
- Stochastic rounding often reduced NaNs but increased perplexity. Maybe it injects noise that breaks deterministic spike pattern.
- Some seeds produce repeated tiny positive biases in layernorm outputs prior to quant which accumulate and occasionally create spike. Worth re-checking layernorm implementation in quant path (folded bias?).

Attachments/what I saved
- token_trace_seed42_exp01.json (saved sequence of token ids up to NaN)
- logits_dump_layer2_int8.bin (raw float32 after dequant step captured by debug kernel)
- per_layer_histograms_seed42.txt (ascii histograms)

Immediate ask from infra/runtime folks
- Can you build a special debug runtime with a dequant sanity assert (print first 64 entries) and a path that logs the raw int32 accumulator values? I will run on dev-gpu-03 and attach outputs.

If I had to bet right now
- 60% kernel bug in optimized int8 path (accumulator/scale ordering or broken upcast)
- 30% calibration tail issue exposing the bug only with rare activations
- 10% fp8 exponent/subnormal mishandling

Short-term mitigation plan
- Canary deploy: enable auto-fallback to BF16 for requests where per-token pre-softmax max exceeds threshold (e.g., >200). Add monitoring alerts for fallbacks.
- Regression test: include the saved token trace as a unit test in runtime test-suite (runs in CI on CPU/GPU emulation).

End of notes — will add more after kernel debug run.

Timestamped quick edits
- 2024-11-09 11:12: created initial notes
- 2024-11-11 09:40: added trial matrix and hypotheses
- 2024-12-02 15:30: observed dequanted 1.545e35 values (suspicious)
